title: Snoop Dogg Criticized for Pre-Inauguration Performance
htmlContent:
Snoop Dogg, a rapper and entrepreneur, has recently come under fire for performing at the Crypto Ball, a pre-inauguration event held in Washington, D.C., before Donald Trump's January 20 swearing-in ceremony. The event, held at the Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium, was organized by former PayPal COO David Sacks to celebrate President Trump's presidency and his administration's pro-crypto stance.

Fans React with Shock and Outrage

Social media quickly responded to Snoop Dogg's attendance at the event. Fans reacted to The Shade Room's video of Snoop on stage with Rick Ross and Soulja Boy with a wave of criticism. Several comments expressed disappointment and anger, with many describing the performance as a betrayal. According to a user, "This is culturally embarrassing and disrespectful," while another remarked, "Not a check in the world worth selling my soul to the Devil…" Prominent figures weighed in on the controversy. On his live stream, Lemon LIVE at 5, Don Lemon addressed the situation, asking whether Snoop and other artists at the event were involved. "sellouts [or] grifters who only care about a dollar."

Amanda Seales Calls Out Snoop's Hypocrisy

Actress and activist Amanda Seales added fuel to the fire by posting a video mash-up juxtaposing Snoop's Crypto Ball performance.
A years-old clip shows the rapper pondering which artist would be the first to perform for Trump. In an old Instagram video, Snoop promised to roast the person who took that step, expressing disdain for the idea. After sharing the updated context, Seales captioned her post. "I hope it's worth it."
The backlash rekindled Snoop's anti-Trump sentiments. In July 2016, the rapper posted a video to Instagram featuring YG and the late Nipsey Hussle's protest anthem, 'FDT' (F*** Donald Trump), where he explicitly voiced his opposition to the then-presidential candidate. Furthermore, Snoop Dogg's 2019 remarks during the government shutdown criticized those who supported Trump, calling them stupid for doing so during tough times.

Mixed Messaging from Snoop

Snoop's decision to perform at the Crypto Ball, even though he has criticized Trump repeatedly, caused many fans to question his motives. To date, he has not publicly commented on his appearance. Reposting an Instagram story featuring himself and Rick Ross at the event, he added more uncertainty to his position.

Community Work Amid Controversy

Snoop Dogg has been giving back to his community despite controversy surrounding his motivations. A donation drive was conducted at his Snoopermarket in Inglewood, California to collect essential items for those affected by the devastating L.A. Days prior to the Crypto Ball wildfires.

What Is the Crypto Ball?

The Crypto Ball's official website describes it as a “celebratory setting,” aimed to honor Trump as “America’s first ‘crypto president.’” An audience of influential figures from the tech and entertainment industries attended the event that showcased the administration's favorable approach to cryptocurrency.

The Fallout and Snoop’s Silence

The reaction to Snoop Dogg's performance at the Crypto Ball highlights the complexity of celebrity endorsements and political alignment. The rapper's popularity as a cultural icon and community advocate is unshaken, but his appearance at an event celebrating Trump has caused fans to question his authenticity. As the controversy progresses, it's up to Snoop to respond to the criticism or let his actions speak for themselves.
